evidence: The strict project privacy policy defaults to offline-only provider egress, remote telemetry disabled, local diagnostic retention, manual document retention, and explicit cache-deletion limitations. Non-offline policy requires the exact project, provider mode, disclosure revision, and informed acknowledgement before an append-only compare-and-swap update.

Project-session authority is required for reads and mutations. Cache clear uses a current one-time preview, rechecks stable file identity and containment, excludes canonical documents and durable database state, denies redirected roots, and reports logical removal separately from best-effort physical erasure.

The approved Project Settings workflow states what will and will not leave the device, requires explicit acknowledgement for egress, offers task-specific provider preview, keeps telemetry off, avoids automatic document deletion, and discloses filesystem limitations without overclaiming secure deletion.

The 37-test security suite and nine focused privacy/contract cases exercise expected policy and cache-clear paths plus consent denial, stale revisions, restart persistence, cross-project/session denial, redirected cache roots, stale preview, canonical-data exclusion, audit redaction, and physical-erasure non-overclaim.
